name: AX30G Chorus, measured 2026-09-16
notes: Six normal-set captures (2026-09-16 10:35-10:46) and two LFO-set captures (30 s tone, 11:00-11:02), all IN-LIN, channel 0 unless stated. Method: the capture's own reference channel through models/ax30g-chain.json is the dry basis, so nothing depends on regenerating the played signal set; a two-tap least-squares fit (sinc-interpolated linear correlation, fractional lag and delay) gives the unit latency, the static delay and the two mix gains at once.

static delay: 939 device samples. Two-tap fit on the Depth-0 capture, 938.975 device samples at 39062.5 Hz on the sweep, 938.988 on the DI clip and 938.975 on the clicks (L and R identical); matched-filter delay of the echo at all four clicks 24.0387-24.0388 ms = 939.01-939.02 samples. 939/39062.5 = 24.0384 ms. Not a round number of displayed ms (24 ms x 39 samples/ms = 936, three samples short), and the Chorus has no delay-time parameter, so it is carried as a constant map rather than through maps.delay's samples_per_ms law.
unit latency in the same fit: 0.2546 ms (sweep and DI), 0.2539 ms (clicks), against the 0.2549 ms measured from the Bypass capture on 2026-09-14. Not part of this model; the chain stage carries it.

mix: fixed, dry 0.75 / wet 0.25. Sharpest measurement is a PER-BAND two-tap fit on the sweep (both gains fitted independently inside each band): wet minus dry is -9.534 / -9.544 / -9.545 / -9.546 / -9.546 / -9.546 / -9.546 / -9.545 / -9.545 / -9.546 / -9.543 dB in the eleven bands from 80 Hz to 19 kHz, mean -9.5455 dB = 0.33326 against 0.25/0.75 = 0.33333 (0.02 % apart) and constant to 0.013 dB across the whole passband. Whole-segment fits agree: wet/dry 0.33187 (sweep), 0.33357 (clicks), 0.33349 (DI) on L and 0.33219 / 0.33402 / 0.33356 on R. Absolute gains against the chained reference were dry 0.3794 / wet 0.1259 (sweep, L), i.e. dry+wet = 0.5053; that 0.5053 is the unit's own output gain and is absorbed by the null test's single gain fit, so the model carries the normalized pair. The dry gain read 0.3779-0.3804 (0.07 dB spread) on all eight captures, so the mix does not move with Speed or Depth.

L and R are the same signal: R = L x +0.0332 dB (sweep), +0.0366 (sine20), +0.0333 (DI), +0.0309 (noise), best time offset 0.0000 samples in every case, and the residual after one gain sits 51-65 dB below R. Mod1 is mono in / mono out and both outputs carry the identical mono result; the 0.03 dB is the interface's channel-gain difference, not the unit.

no feedback. A 3-tap and a 4-tap least-squares fit on the sweep put the taps at 2D and 3D at -87.0 and -88.4 dB against the wet tap's -18.0 dB, i.e. 69 dB below the first echo and no better than the fit's own floor; in the click windows of the Depth-0 capture the first echo peaks at -38.6 dBFS while the 46-51 ms window (where a second echo would land) reads -83.6 dBFS against a -82.3 dBFS floor measured at 100-140 ms. Exactly one echo. blocks.lfo.in_loop is therefore moot and is set false.

no damping on the wet path. The per-band two-tap fit above IS the measurement: wet minus dry is flat to 0.013 dB from 80 Hz to 19 kHz, with no low-pass shape anywhere, and the per-band nulls run -59.6 dB at 630-1250 Hz to -38.3 dB at 17-19 kHz. A cruder independent check (deconvolving the fitted dry and wet components separately against the reference over the noise segment, 11 log bands) gives wet minus dry of -0.79 / -0.71 / -0.41 / -0.42 / 0.00 / -0.45 / -0.12 / +0.01 / -0.06 / +0.95 / +0.52 dB at 113 Hz to 18 kHz, agreeing within its own scatter. A flat-gain two-tap model nulls the sweep at -30.0 dB, which a filtered wet path would not allow.

modulation is UNIPOLAR ABOVE the static delay, as in MODD and SMOD. Absolute delay during the tone (phase of the wet residual against the dry reference, unwrapped with the integrated trajectory): minimum minus the Depth-0 static delay is +0.0004 ms at Depth 10, +0.0025 at Depth 50 / Speed 1, +0.0163 at Depth 50 / Speed 5, and +0.0010 at Depth 25 / Speed 1 (robust 0.05 percentile) -- 0.02 to 0.6 device samples above the static value out of swings of 102 to 511 samples. Independently, all 24 click readings across the six modulated captures lie above the static 24.0384 ms (minimum 24.2161 ms), which under a bipolar hypothesis would happen with probability about 2^-24.

depth: linear through the origin, borrowed from MODD unchanged (out_max 6.5247 ms amplitude at Depth 50). CHO's own measurement, by 256-bin synchronous average of the delay trajectory at the fitted rate, in device samples at this model's 39062.5 Hz: p-p 255.178 at Depth 25 (10.2071 per Depth unit) and 509.675 at Depth 50 (10.1935 per unit), mean 10.2003 against MODD's stored 10.1935 -- 0.07 % apart. Against the MODD map the predicted p-p is 254.87 samples at Depth 25 (measured 255.178, difference 0.31) and 509.74 at Depth 50 (measured 509.675, difference 0.06). The independent absolute-phase method gives 2.6173 / 6.5468 / 13.0645 / 13.0911 ms p-p at Depth 10 / 25 (Speed 1) / 50 (Speed 5) / 50 (Speed 1), i.e. 0.2617 / 0.2619 / 0.2613 / 0.2618 ms per Depth unit -- linear through the origin over the whole range. At Depth 0 the trajectory p-p is 0.0003 ms, so the modulation really does stop.

speed: MODD's 12-point table borrowed unchanged. Measured on the 30 s tone (29 and 145 LFO cycles in the window): Speed 1 -> 0.996452 Hz against the table's 0.9965 (-48 ppm), Speed 5 -> 4.989770 against 4.989728 (+8 ppm). The normal set's 4 s tone holds only 3 cycles at Speed 1 and its rate fits scatter over 0.9853-0.9974 Hz; Speed 0.2 has 0.6 cycles in that window and was NOT measured -- an LFO-set capture at Speed 0.2 would settle it.

LFO waveform: MODD's 256-point table, unchanged. The 256-bin synchronous average of each CHO trajectory, normalized to [0,1] with its minimum rolled to index 0, differs from the stored MODD table by 0.00109 rms of swing at Speed 1 / Depth 25 (0.278 device samples, 7.1 us) and 0.00031 at Speed 5 / Depth 50 (0.160 samples, 4.1 us), while a sine differs by 0.04502 / 0.04462 and a triangle by 0.04035 / 0.04080. The two CHO cycles agree with each other to 0.00138. Harmonics of the measured cycle: 3rd/1st -24.90 dB and 5th/1st -34.45 dB in both, against MODD's own -24.91 and -34.43. Same LFO block as the Mod Delay.
read interpolation: linear, as MODD and SMOD.

sample_rate 39062.5 (SUPERSEDED 2026-09-16, see below) -- this model ran at the HARDWARE rate, unlike ax30g-sdly/modd/smod which null at the fitted 39057.15. Reason: the Chorus' static delay is an exact integer 939 device samples, and only the true device rate keeps it integer. Measured null of the Depth-0 capture, overall / sine20 / sweep: 39062.5 with delay 939 -> -31.4 / -59.0 / -34.7 dB; 39057.15 with delay 938.87 (the same wall-clock 24.038 ms) -> -28.9 / -57.6 / -29.4; 39062.5 with delay 938.87 -> -29.8 / -48.3 / -30.8. The 2.5 dB is the delay line's linear interpolation: at a fractional read it low-passes, at frac 0 it does not. A whole sample out (938 at 39062.5) costs 15 dB on the sweep two-tap fit (-14.8 against -29.8), so 939 is unambiguous.

clock tension worth recording (now resolved, see below): the CHO delay measurement implies a device rate of 939/0.02403776 s = 39063.4 Hz, while the 2026-09-14 SDLY scan (11700 samples measured as 299.561 ms at a 300 ms setting) implied 39057.2 -- 160 ppm apart. Over the Chorus' 939 samples that difference is 0.13 samples and does not accumulate; over SDLY's 11700 it is 1.6. Not resolved here; both models keep the rate that nulls their own captures best.

2026-09-16: sample_rate 39062.5 -> 39063.829787 (effective 153/188 of 48 kHz), delay left at the constant 939 device samples (unaffected by the samples_per_ms law, so no offset_samples here). This is the rate the 2026-09-16 SDLY clock note found nulls all four of its SDLY captures at or near their own best (docs/sdly-clock-2026-09-16.md, 'Adopted 2026-09-16') -- and it resolves the clock-tension note above: 39063.83 sits almost exactly on this model's own independent 939/0.02403776s = 39063.4 Hz estimate from the Chorus delay alone (0.4 Hz / 10 ppm apart), where the old pairing (39062.5 CHO vs 39057.15 SDLY) was 160 ppm apart. Regression: Depth-0 capture null overall -31.4 -> -31.3 dB (unchanged, sub-noise) -- see the null table in docs/sdly-clock-2026-09-16.md.
